note: Information cards for selectable landmarks. Every fact names its source; where a value is rounded or a location is approximate, the card says so. Keys match the 'n' field in landmarks.json. Sources are public references cited as citations, not fetched at runtime.

facts: 167 m (548 ft) to the top of the William Penn statue
11 m (37 ft) bronze William Penn by Alexander Milne Calder
The tallest habitable building in the world until 1908
Philadelphia City Hall.text: Second Empire masonry at Broad and Market streets. The schematic model includes the courtyard, corner pavilions and tower at its published overall height.

Independence Hall.text: Georgian brick on the gentle rise above the Delaware waterfront. The model here is schematic: a hall with two wings and a steeple at the published height.

facts: Faire Mount, the bluff where the Schuylkill turns toward Center City
Greek Revival temple front on a podium
72, the ones made famous by Rocky
Philadelphia Museum of Art.text: Three temple-fronted pavilions on a podium at the head of the Benjamin Franklin Parkway. The model is a schematic podium and pavilions, not a survey of the building.

facts: A row of rowing-club boathouses on the east bank of the Schuylkill
Boathouse Row.text: Just above the Fairmount Dam, where the tidal Schuylkill ends. The model is a schematic row of gabled houses; the real row has more houses of more shapes.

facts: about 341 m as measured in OpenStreetMap; 342 m (1,121 ft) published
Comcast Technology Center.text: Drawn from its real OpenStreetMap footprint at its measured height, like every other building on the map. The stepped model and facade ribs are schematic.

Citizens Bank Park.text: The ballpark at the South Philadelphia sports complex, on reclaimed low ground near the Navy Yard. OpenStreetMap maps the stadium as a leisure area with no height, so the map draws a schematic bowl at a published height.

Lincoln Financial Field.text: The football stadium of the sports complex. Like the ballpark it is drawn as a schematic bowl: the real building is an open-ended horseshoe of stands.

facts: 2001, as a museum ship on the Camden waterfront
Battleship New Jersey.text: Moored on the Camden side of the Delaware opposite Penn's Landing. The hull and superstructure here are a schematic at the published length; the mooring position is approximate to a few tens of metres.

facts: held out for about six weeks against the Royal Navy in autumn 1777
Mud Island, in the Delaware marshes below the airport
Fort Mifflin.text: A star-shaped bastioned fort at the water's edge. The model is a schematic ring of low walls; the real plan is a stone-faced star.

facts: 533 m (1,750 ft), the world's longest suspension span until 1929
I-676 / US 30 and the PATCO line
Benjamin Franklin Bridge.text: Deck alignment and width from OpenStreetMap; towers, cables and hangers are drawn schematically from published dimensions.

Walt Whitman Bridge.text: The southern suspension crossing, from South Philadelphia to Gloucester City. Schematic form from published dimensions.

facts: roughly 60 m from creek to upland in this map's elevation data
Wissahickon Valley.text: A gorge cut into the Piedmont entirely inside the city. The depth quoted is what this map's DEM shows, not a surveyed figure.

facts: the Schuylkill Navigation canal opened here in 1819
from the Lenape word for the river, 'place to drink'
the Manayunk Wall, Lyceum Avenue, famous from the bicycle race
Manayunk.text: Steep streets climbing from the Schuylkill where the valley narrows.

facts: filled tidal flats on the Delaware; among the lowest land in the region
Philadelphia Int'l Airport.text: Its runways sit within a few metres of sea level in this map's elevation data.

facts: Valley Forge National Historical Park, since 1976
where Valley Creek meets the Schuylkill, between Mount Joy and Mount Misery
Valley Forge.text: The hills that sheltered the encampment read clearly in the relief.

facts: the flat Delaware terrace downstream of the falls at Trenton
Levittown.text: The archetypal postwar planned suburb. Its houses are outside the map's building zones, so only the terrain and roads are drawn here.

facts: the flat Delaware waterfront shelf north-east of Center City
a historic river neighbourhood of rowhouse blocks and rail yards
Port Richmond.text: Inside the inner-city building zone, so its notable buildings are drawn; the rowhouse fabric is not.

Cira Centre.text: Beside 30th Street Station on the west bank of the Schuylkill, drawn from its OpenStreetMap footprint at its measured height.

facts: Aquariums, fish, reef and pond supplies
The Hidden Reef.text: A local aquarium destination in Levittown. The pin uses the OpenStreetMap store point within its commercial building footprint.
